title: Waves of IMF lending
summary: The number of countries living under an IMF arrangement rose and fell in waves. It peaked at 75 countries in 1996. Each country is coloured by the period in which it spent the most years under IMF arrangements, which shows which wave pulled it in: the debt crisis of the 1980s and early 1990s, the transition and Asian crises to 2007, or the global and euro-area crises from 2008. Emergency and rapid payouts are left out because they carry few conditions.

title: Sold off, then taken back
summary: From 1988 to 2008 the World Bank recorded 10,193 sales and handovers of state firms and services in 124 low- and middle-income countries, with the most in 1998 (1796). From 2000 the Public Futures database records 1,787 cases of towns, regions and countries taking services back from private firms or setting up new public ones, most of them in Europe and North America. Countries are coloured by whether they appear in one record or both. In 55 countries services were sold under the first wave and some were later taken back.
